text:
mika: heads up — after the kernel-selection tweak yesterday i'm seeing a subtle host-side p99 bump for short streaming requests (<=64 tokens). digging into tokenization + preparse. anyone else seeing this?

devon: yeah saw an uptick in our perf dashboard around 21:10 UTC. looks like CPU time in the proto unpack path increased. not sure if grpc framing change or our new async chunker.

ryan: fwiw the KV-cache hit rate is unchanged for those flows, so feels like a pure host parse/tokenize cost. attached quick flame:
```
python profiler: host_preparse :: self 42% | tokenize 26% | proto_deser 18% | socket_read 8% | other 6%
```

aj: hmm — tokenization moving into async chunker could add a small context switch. are we double-copying the buffer?

mika: good call. i grepped and found one `memcpy` in the chunker + one in the proto shim. patch at line: `grpc_streamer.cc:145` doing `append(buf)` then later `slice.copy()` during proto unpack.

leah: can we short-circuit for the small-request fastpath? e.g., if content-length < 256 and single-chunk do zero-copy path.

devon: +1. also the kernel selection change increased typical seq_len estimate which triggers a different decode kernel that expects larger KV cache prefetch windows. might be causing slightly heavier host preproc due to extra header work.

mika: i ran a quick canary with zero-copy and p99 dropped back ~1.5ms -> 0.8ms on small streams. still investigating edge cases. patch here (local):
```
// fastpath: avoid slice.copy for small single-chunk frames
if (frame.size() <= 256 && frame.is_single_chunk()) {
  proto_view = frame.view(); // no copy
} else {
  proto_view = frame.copy();
}
```

infra-bot: deploy 4990012300 -> eng-runtime canary succeeded (10/10 hosts), telemetry flagged host-preparse p99 regressions on canary-8.

ryan: canary telemetry matches — interesting that only canary-8 saw the spike. maybe kernel-to-host affinity on that pool.

aj: could be NUMA layout or NIC interrupt core pinning. can we grab `perf top` while reproducing small stream?

mika: collecting `perf` traces now and a lightweight syscall summary. i'll drop artifacts in the perf bucket and post link.

leah: for rollout plan — short-term revert kernel estimate change or gate it behind a flag? we should also add a microbenchmark for small streaming path in CI.

mika: agree. plan: 1) add zero-copy fastpath in chunker (patch ready), 2) add microbenchmark and perf test, 3) run targeted canary across different host pools, 4) if still regressing revert kernel estimate tweak. i'll open PR and ping @devon for review.

devon: sounds good. thanks for triage. :thumbsup:

mika: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/4123 (draft) — tests running. will update this thread with perf numbers and the perf bucket link.

ryan: thanks — if you want i can trigger a perf-aware canary that sweeps NIC/NUMA variants.

mika: please do, that would help rule out pool-specific config.

infra-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/4990012345/trace-20260315.tar.gz

mika: got the traces. initial `perf` shows syscall time in `recvmsg` unchanged, main spike is in `tokenizer::process` (with increased allocations). looks like the copy avoided for most flows but allocations still happen on fastpath due to temp string construction. working on reusing buffers.

leah: nice. once buffer reuse is in place let's run 24h canary before wide rollout.

mika: will do. thanks everyone.
